text: The staging cluster runs Kubernetes version 1.29.
Our main API is written in Go and deployed as a container.
The team uses trunk-based development with short-lived branches.
Code reviews require at least one approval before merging.
The default branch is called main.
I prefer tabs over spaces in Go projects.
Unit tests run in GitHub Actions on every pull request.
The production database is PostgreSQL 15 on a managed instance.
We store build artifacts in an S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
My laptop runs Ubuntu 22.04 with 32 GB of RAM.
The frontend is built with Next.js and TypeScript.
I like to keep functions under 40 lines.
Our on-call rotation changes every Monday morning.
The monitoring dashboard is hosted in Grafana.
I use Neovim as my main editor.
Dependencies are pinned with a lock file in every repository.
The staging database is refreshed from production every Sunday.
Our logging format is JSON with a request id field.
I work mostly on the payments service.
Feature flags are managed through a small internal service.
I always use virtual environments when working on Python projects.
Never commit directly to main in our team.
Whenever I deploy, I run the smoke tests first.
From now on I am using Rust for new command-line tools.
If a build fails twice, I usually check the dependency cache first.
When I review pull requests I start with the tests.
I always write the migration before changing the model.
Our team lead asked everyone to update their local tools this week.
Our manager approved the new on-call schedule last Friday.
The security team reviewed the dependency list and found no issues.
I prefer to remove unused imports before committing.
We delete old log files after thirty days according to the retention policy.
I run rm -i when cleaning temporary files so it asks before deleting.
Please remember that I work in the Pacific time zone.
The admin console is only available through the company VPN.
I disabled the unused feature flag in the staging environment.
My teammate Priya maintains the CI pipeline.
I use curl to test our health check endpoint.
We use eval only inside the sandboxed notebook environment.
The CI pipeline caches node modules between runs.
